title: Augmented oracles (x-, y-, full-point, halving, endomorphism-image, incidence) and GGM simulability
mechanism: Give the solver an extra public oracle (x-coordinate, y-coordinate, full point, halving query, endomorphism image, factor-base incidence, jet) and hope it supplies sub-birthday information or guided decomposition.

title: Coordinate-statistic hunts: bias of x/y, slopes, bits, cross-ratios and trace functions under the group law
mechanism: Search for a cheap coordinate statistic (Legendre/cubic residue, low bits, digit sums, chord/tangent slopes, cross-ratios, trace-function sheaves) whose behaviour under P -> P+Q or P -> 2P is non-random and concentrates on a cheaply decidable subset, so a coordinate distinguisher leaks into key recovery (RQ-ECDLP-4fcbd3, the CRYPTO census).

title: GOAL-CRYPTO-001 discovery screen for a reproducible non-generic crypto-size algorithm
mechanism: Screen literature and representation families (compact target-label common factors, defect-scaled hyperplane-signature zero-minor routes, corner-coefficient induction, KN-OPEN gates) through Gate A/B admission for any candidate that could beat rho on cryptographic prime-field ECDLP.

title: Alternative curve models and point representations (Edwards, Hessian, Montgomery, Kummer, x-only)
mechanism: Change the model or coordinate (Edwards, Hessian, Jacobi, Montgomery, Kummer line, theta coordinates, twist cosets) so that summation polynomials, membership tests or collision arithmetic become cheaper.

title: Additive-character bias of the discrete log on structured factor bases (H-PSEUDO)
mechanism: If max_k |sum_{P in F} e(2 pi i k DL(P)/N)| over the small-x set F were well above sqrt(B), the factor base would have super-random additive yield; by the Betti-yield duality (KN-FIND-9d2f56) exactly this is what a sub-rho combinatorial IC needs.

title: Elliptic nets / elliptic divisibility sequences as a relation or annihilator source
mechanism: Re-encode kP through the Shipsey/Stange elliptic net W(a,b) (division-polynomial values) and use the two-parameter Somos identities, short annihilators or EDS periods as an exact multiplicative relation supply. If net-value collisions or a short annihilator of a target-translated block arrived below the birthday bound, index calculus on net exponents would beat BSGS/rho.

title: Wagner k-tree / four-list joins with cheap sum-compatible filters
mechanism: Run a Wagner-style k-list tree (or representation-technique subset-sum) on E(F_p) using a cheap filter h with h(P+Q)=f(h(P),h(Q)) often enough, or an output-sensitive partial verifier, aiming at N^(1/3+o(1)) end-to-end. Signed-y and Boolean-success cascades are the program's concrete instances.

title: Height-compressing global lifts (Q, number fields, function fields / elliptic surfaces)
mechanism: Lift E/F_p and the factor base to a curve over Q, a special number field (SNFS/Solinas/cyclotomic) or an elliptic surface over F_p(t), find short Mordell-Weil relations there, and reduce them back. A lift whose relations stay short (bounded height) would give relations for free; xedni calculus is the classical instance.

title: Hashed-factor-base ECDL with a compact low-degree Boolean encoding and exact tensor contraction (Akshima et al., Bochum v0.2), conditional on the openai/math #k
mechanism: Akshima et al., "A Subexponential Time Algorithm for Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm" (Bochum v0.2, pinned 1ee44e56), hash-select a factor base and encode relation finding as a compact low-degree Boolean system (ripple arithmetic, Fourier integer products, affine hashes, cofactor clearing). They solve it by exact tensor contraction with the recursive counting backend of the openai/math ETH prepr

title: Bit-security / hidden-number conversion of DL leakage, auxiliary inputs and advice
mechanism: Turn any weak correlation between public coordinates and bits of the logarithm (or leaked auxiliary inputs [alpha^i]G, or stored advice) into full DL recovery via hidden-number-problem lattices or Cheon-style divisor walks. A conversion with exponent 2*beta below 1/2 would make a small statistic advantage an attack.

title: 'ECDLP-IDEA breakthrough corpus: algebraic-geometric transforms awaiting constructors'
mechanism: The ideas/ECDLP-IDEA-* corpus (about 436 generated ideas: spinor-matchgate addition transform, block-Krylov transition intersection, Cremona-shrunk toric decomposition, aggregate complement-divisor compression, x-only nonfaithful signed lifts, conormal-polar blowups, ramification-break digits, and many more) proposes representation changes whose payoff depends on an explicit constructor or theorem

title: The invertible half: dense, cheaply recognizable AND cheaply invertible subsets of E(F_p)
mechanism: Find D subset E(F_p) with |D| >= n^alpha (alpha > 1/2) whose membership is decidable from coordinates and whose logs are computable from coordinates (a "hint family"), e.g. a low-degree polynomial agreeing with log_g on the small-x set. Random self-reduction into D would then beat the square-root bound; failing that, a provable recognizable/invertible duality would close the lane.

title: Lossy tracked objects propagated through scalar multiplication (doubling coordinates, rigidity, belief propagation)
mechanism: Track a lossy function of the point (x+y, xy, doubling slope, low bits, residue symbols, split-quotient certificates, latent linear embeddings) through the double-and-add chain and prune scalars by constraint/belief propagation, hoping the object propagates cheaply while still reading the instance.

title: Program methodology: instrument calibration, nulls, findings promotion (not a cost mechanism)
mechanism: Records that test the program's own instruments (label-permutation nulls, planted-signal controls, detection floors, solving-degree meters), its findings-promotion gate and its record integrity. They decide whether other leads' negatives and positives are trustworthy; they cannot by themselves make ECDLP cheaper.

title: Miller functions, S-unit descent and pairing-free Miller cocycles on prime-order curves
mechanism: Use Miller functions f_{N,P}, their S-unit supports, generalized-Jacobian extension classes or a partial pairing "return cycle" to map points to a multiplicative group without a small embedding degree. When gcd(N,p-1)=1 the N-th root U(R)=f(R)^(1/N) is a canonical primitive of the Miller cocycle and is computable from R; if U(kP) exposed k through a cheap closed form, the DLP would move to F_p^*.

title: Machine learning / neural and RL approaches to ECDLP and its subroutines
mechanism: Learn a predictor of log bits, a latent linearisation of the group law, a solver branching policy, an isogeny-class walk policy (RL) or a curve-hardness predictor, and use it to prune search or pick cheaper presentations.

title: Prime-to-p jets, canonical/Teichmuller lifts and p-adic formal-group digits
mechanism: Lift points to F_p[eps]/eps^2, Z/p^2 or E(Q_p) (dual-number jets, canonical prime-to-p torsion lifts, Teichmuller or Serre-Tate lifts) and read a formal-group logarithm or valuation digit that is linear in the scalar, extending the anomalous (Smart/Satoh-Araki) channel to non-anomalous curves.

title: Quantum ECDLP: reversible secp256k1 point-addition circuits for Shor (resource reduction)
mechanism: Reduce Toffoli count x peak qubits of the reversible point-addition circuit that dominates Shor's ECDLP algorithm on secp256k1 (dialog-GCD affine adder, Karatsuba/Solinas squaring). This lowers the fault-tolerant cost of a known polynomial-time quantum attack; it does not change classical cost and has no matched-rho comparison.

title: Split-Jacobian projected smoothness and the pair (P,Q) as a genus-2 divisor
mechanism: Embed E into a split abelian surface / genus-2 Jacobian (gluing, Poincare factor) or encode (P,Q) as one Mumford divisor, hoping that projected divisors are smooth more often than points of E so that genus-2 index calculus applies to the elliptic factor.

title: Torsor, deck-orbit, cubical/biextension and scalar-orbit elliptic-period descent
mechanism: Place the instance on a G_m/G_a-torsor or a Galois cover over E (cubical lifts, biextensions, theta structures, level-N linearisation) and use deck-group orbits or an elliptic period of the scalar orbit as a public label that routes the target to a small fibre.

title: Variants of the advice table: batch-reselected, batch-grown, basin-instrumented and transported tables
mechanism: Re-select or grow a Bernstein-Lange table from the batch's own solved walks, measure coverage as exact basin sizes, or carry a table across isogenous curves, hoping to match a static table with less precomputation or reuse one table on many curves.

title: 'Rho on automorphism/Frobenius orbits: sqrt(2m) on Koblitz, order-4/6 maps on j=1728/j=0'
mechanism: An efficiently computable automorphism group of order A lets rho walk on orbits and divides the expected steps by sqrt(A): signed Frobenius on Koblitz curves (A = 2m), GLV automorphisms of order 4 or 6 on j=1728 and j=0 prime curves. The cost is a per-step canonicalisation.

title: Batched affine steps: Montgomery simultaneous inversion and the free x(P-Q) beside x(P+Q)
mechanism: Montgomery's trick replaces n inversions by one plus about 3(n-1) multiplications, and x(P-Q) shares the slope denominator of x(P+Q). Both make affine parallel rho cheap per step.

title: Step to the better of k candidate images (best of P+R, P-R) to concentrate in-degree
mechanism: Choosing the best-scoring of k candidate images gives image points in-degree k*u^(k-1), so collisions arrive sqrt(k^2/(2k-1)) sooner (1.155 for k = 2). P+R and P-R share one inversion, so the second candidate costs about 1M+1S; the net depends on how many walks share an inversion.

title: Baby-step giant-step family (textbook, interleaved, negation, paired, signed-Frobenius claw)
mechanism: BSGS variants reach low operation counts (with negation 1.10x the floor at toy size) by storing Theta(sqrt r) points; the claw pair table is a randomised BSGS on signed Frobenius classes.

title: Cheaper step primitives never measured here: tag tracing on EC, point-halving steps on binary curves
mechanism: Tag tracing (Cheon-Hong-Kim) decides most steps from partial information with precomputed tables, skipping full products; point halving can replace addition-based steps on binary curves (Zhang-Wang). Either would lower native cost per step without changing the counted constant.

title: Run Cheon's auxiliary-input algorithm on ordinary ECDLP by generating [x^d]P yourself
mechanism: Cheon recovers x from P, [x]P, [x^d]P in ~sqrt(r/d) + sqrt(d) when d | r-1 (or r+1). If the attacker could produce [x^d]P from (P, [x]P) cheaply, ordinary ECDLP would fall to ~r^{1/4} on curves with a good divisor.

title: Where Cheon stops on deployed parameters: exact r+-1 divisor census times priced auxiliary supply
mechanism: With the divisor lattices of r-1 and r+1 for standardized orders, E(r) = min_d log(sqrt((r+-1)/d) + sqrt(d))/log r says how far Cheon could go; a typed supply roster (powers-of-tau SRS, q-SDH and VRF query channels) says which degree d any protocol actually releases.

title: Toy reproduction of Cheon's algorithm with memory charged and supplied-input CRT composition
mechanism: Reproduce Cheon's r-1 and r+1 branches at 40-64-bit r with stage 1 as a parallel collision search (memory charged), planted-divisor curves with a no-divisor null, and CRT composition of several supplied first-stage residues.

title: 'Correlated walks: one shared index sequence or shared precomputed sums across walks'
mechanism: Let all parallel walks follow one index sequence, or step by precomputed sums R_i + R_j, so that table work is shared and each addition advances more than one step.

title: Distinguished points, multi-target batching and Bernstein-Lange precomputation (incumbent controls)
mechanism: van Oorschot-Wiener DPs give linear parallel speedup with small memory; solving L targets with a shared DP table costs ~sqrt(2Ln); a precomputed table of ~l^{1/3} DPs gives l^{1/3} online cost. These are the incumbents every 'advice' or batch comparison must beat.

title: ECC2K-130 kernel throughput on GPU and FPGA (iterations per second per device and per watt)
mechanism: At fixed iterations, solve cost is set by updates per second: bitsliced normal-basis arithmetic, native carry-less products, batch inversion geometry, shared-memory sigma tables. FPGAs lay the same bit operations out in space.

title: 'ECC2K-130 iteration function: sigma walk vs v3 table walk vs class-signed sigma steps'
mechanism: The campaign walks R <- R + sigma^j(R) (injective penalty c ~ 1.07). A table walk R + eps sigma^k(T_h) runs 9-15% faster per update; a class-derived sign (SIGMA_SIGN=2) cuts the branch-probability penalty. Each change starts a new DP corpus, so the choice is made once.

title: Beat the square-root exponent with any generic collision algorithm
mechanism: Any algorithm that uses only group operations and equality tests (rho, kangaroo, BSGS, grumpy giants, multi-walk, GPU variants) is a generic algorithm. If one of them could find logs in o(sqrt r) operations, every curve would weaken at once.

title: Exact average-case constant of store-all generic schedules (grumpy giants, compiled tiered walks)
mechanism: Two grumpy giants and a baby (and adaptive or compiled store-everything schedules) solve more targets per operation than BSGS or a random walk (0.71875 vs 0.6753 at 1.5 sqrt l). Theorem A makes the solved set target-independent, so the mean is an exact integer ratio.

title: Kangaroo / lambda (van Oorschot-Wiener, Gaudry-Schost) as a full-group ECDLP solver
mechanism: Kangaroo methods solve an interval DLP of width N in ~2 sqrt(N) and run with distinguished points; applied to the whole group they compete with rho.

title: Residue-guess price of modular (mod-M) representation filters in prime-order groups
mechanism: Subset-sum techniques (Schroeppel-Shamir, BCJ, Esser-May) filter partial sums by a congruence mod M. In a prime-order group the residue of a partial log is not visible, so each filter must guess it; the claim is that every algorithm of class F_M pays the multiplier G_M = |rho_M(W)|.

title: 'Low-Hamming-weight DLP with polynomial memory: collision walks on the weight-w class'
mechanism: For a log of bit-length m and weight w, meet-in-the-middle reaches sqrt(binom(m, w)) with large memory; a collision walk whose states are low-weight representations (jump sums, carry-run mixtures, nonbacktracking lifts) could reach it with polylog memory.

title: 'Low-weight DLP with preprocessing: the (P, S, T, epsilon, U) frontier'
mechanism: Advice tables (Coppersmith-split tables, Bernstein-Lange style DP tables restricted to low-weight logs) could trade precomputation for online time on the low-weight class.

title: 'The matched rho reference itself: finite-size bias and the missing prime medium tier'
mechanism: Every IC row and every rho variant is ranked against a matched rho reference. Toy rho bounds carry fixed set-up costs (fitted alpha 0.31-0.45 below 0.5), and the sealed frontier has a medium-tier domain for Koblitz curves only. A calibrated prime medium-tier rho bound would fix the denominator of every prime-field gap.

title: 'Native cost of one rho step: canonicalisation, field arithmetic and admitted CPU timing'
mechanism: GAE counts group additions; the native step also pays class canonicalisation (Koblitz rotations, counted but not charged), modular reduction and branch behaviour. Cutting instructions per step speeds every walk without changing the counted constant.

title: Negation-map rho on {+-P} classes with fruitless-cycle escape (prime curves)
mechanism: Walking on x-coordinate classes {P, -P} halves the state space and should save sqrt(2) in steps, but makes 2-cycles (and longer fruitless cycles) that trap walks unless an escape rule is used. The constant the program pays depends on the escape rule and the r-adding table size.

title: 'Equivalence classes larger than Aut(E): quotients by subgroups H of (Z/N)^*'
mechanism: Rho could walk on classes {[h]P : h in H} for a subgroup H of (Z/N)^* larger than the automorphism group. The gain would be sqrt(|H|) if a class representative (or an H-invariant of the encoding) were cheap; for scalar multipliers that are not automorphisms every canonicalisation costs a scalar multiplication.

title: Distributed pool v2 walk has no class quotient: add negation (sqrt 2) and Frobenius (sqrt 2m)
mechanism: ecc-challenges' generic v2 worker walks plain rho, so a solve expects sqrt(pi n/2) steps on all 23 non-ECC2K-130 campaigns. A negation-map walk saves sqrt(2) on every curve and signed Frobenius saves sqrt(2m) on ECC2K-163/238/358; both are established and reproduced in crypto.

title: GPU rho on prime and generic binary curves with an admitted CPU/GPU comparison
mechanism: Batched affine rho on GPUs (NIST P-256/P-384 kernel, generic Certicom workers) multiplies walk throughput; an admitted ecbench GPU arm would put device results on the same frontier as CPU arms.

title: 'Iteration-function choice: Teske r-adding walks, mixing, hashed partitions'
mechanism: The walk constant depends on how close the iteration function is to a random mapping. r-adding walks with r of 16-20 are near random; a partition read from few bits or a small r costs extra steps.

title: Cofactor-projected factor base ([h]P into the prime-order subgroup) on the random-binary ladder rows with cofactor h > 1
mechanism: The random-binary ladder rows build the factor base from raw curve points with no projection into the prime-order subgroup, so a fraction 1 - 1/h of every negation-folded pair table can never match a subgroup target (measured class-zero fraction 0.50, 0.50, 0.17 at h = 2, 2, 6). title: Spending the cofactor and 2-torsion of binary curves: quotient labels, k-tree filters, 2-torsion translation quotients of the factor base
mechanism: Use E -> E/2E -> E/4E coset labels on legs, homomorphic cofactor quotients or sum-compatible filters (Wagner k-tree) to prune decomposition candidates, or fold the factor base by 2-torsion translation.

title: Composite-degree ANSI X9.62 binary curves (c2pnb176/208/272/304/368): Gaudry-Diem n = 4 with a pi_16 orbit base
mechanism: These curves live over F_{2^{16k}}, so an intermediate subfield exists: fixed-n Gaudry-Diem decomposition with double large primes has an exponent below rho. The question is whether the per-trial cost and memory let it beat matched rho at the deployed sizes.

title: Decomposition-oracle encodings and SAT/enumeration solving of binary PDP: SAT/XOR, Karabina, S_m symmetrisation, chained vs direct S_4, Nagao, basis and reducti
mechanism: Re-present the point-decomposition system (symmetric coordinates, chained S_3 vs direct S_4, Nagao cosets, normal vs polynomial basis, field polynomial) and solve it with SAT/XOR or enumeration, hoping the per-attempt cost grows slower than exhaustive search.

title: ECC2K-130 via a Jacobian carrying the trace-zero abelian variety A (Torelli rarity heuristic)
mechanism: If the 130-dimensional trace-zero part A of Res(E) were isogenous to an evaluable Jacobian of genus 130-300, plane/hyperelliptic IC there would cost about 2^37.2, 23.6 bits below rho. The closure rests on a codimension heuristic (8,128), not a theorem. Shares scope with the transfer family.

title: Choice of the factor-base subspace V at fixed dimension (geometric progression, dim(V.V), trace rank, cosets, greedy coverage, HW pools, trace-parity window)
mechanism: Pick V so that the descended system is sparser (small product space V.V, low trace rank) or so that coverage of targets is higher (greedy, cosets, Hamming-weight pools), lowering cost per relation at the same |F|.

title: Free relations from self-collisions in the pair-root table (no-probe relations)
mechanism: Two pair-states of the compact-orbit table with the same canonical root abscissa are a four-term relation among factor-base points, found by one sort of an existing table; the prediction was ~11,000 relations at n61/K600 and a free rank stage.

title: Frobenius/endomorphism-invariant factor bases and orbit columns on Koblitz and subfield curves, beyond the trivial orbit saving
mechanism: A factor base closed under the q-power Frobenius (or a CM automorphism phi) folds every orbit into one column: relations needed drop by n and linear algebra by n^2. The hope was a second gain in the decomposition step itself, or a cheaper descended system, on top of the orbit fold. It is the incumbent structure of every Koblitz IC row on the leaderboard (compact-orbit base).

title: Frobenius as a symmetry of the decomposition search: orbit CNF encodings, conjugate attempts, equivariant elimination
mechanism: Use x -> x^2 (or tau) as a symmetry inside one decomposition search: symmetry-breaking clauses, orbit-quotient encodings, treating the n conjugates of a target as one attempt, or Faugere-Svartz character blocks in F4, to divide per-attempt cost by up to n.

title: Generic decomposition oracles for Koblitz IC: pair tables, compact-orbit 4-sum, MITM and enumeration, cap-locus arity, known-log pools
mechanism: Decide whether a target is an m-sum of factor-base points by table lookup, pair tables or meet-in-the-middle, collect relations, solve the orbit-folded matrix and descend. This is the production pipeline behind every Table A and Table C row; engineering it (K, arity, table layout) is how the baseline has improved.

title: Co-designed binary factor bases with exact decomposition: affine 2-flats, orbit-canonical abscissa lookup, SAT vs exact MITM (KIC lane)
mechanism: Design the factor base and the decomposition constraint together (affine-plane pools, one-hot shift encodings, orbit-canonical pair lookup with exact witness transport) so that charged decomposition cost drops without losing coverage.

title: The matched Koblitz rho reference for binary IC rows: step pricing, signed-Frobenius canonicalisation, a 131-bit walk
mechanism: Every gap in this family divides by a rho reference. Table A divides by rho as built (32 lanes, 9.7-11.8 units a step) while the canonical step costs 4.6-5.4 and the IC arm gets the 1,024-lane batched unit; normal-basis canonicalisation makes signed-Frobenius rho 4.1x cheaper (cryptanalysis); and no 131-bit walk exists, so no ECC2K-130 lane has a matched rho. title: Cutting the reusable set-up of the one-target Koblitz pipeline (Table A), where 98.5-99.7% of S sits
mechanism: In Table A the target-independent set-up (pair table, relation rank, linear algebra) is 98.5-99.7% of S and the descent at most 1.4%. Constant levers already measured outside the board (per-size K retune, production free relations, orbit fast path, cache-blocked pair-table build) attack exactly that phase. It cannot change the exponent, but every verified cut shrinks the distance to rho.

title: Single and double large-prime relation collection for binary and Koblitz IC (free-leg, GTTD on subspace bases)
mechanism: Accept decompositions with one or two points outside the base and combine partial relations through cycles in a large-prime graph, trading more linear algebra for fewer full decompositions; in the Gaudry-Theriault-Thome-Diem setting it lowers the exponent to q^{2-2/n}. On prime-degree binary subspace bases the free-leg form is a birthday search in the large base.

mechanism: Fit a log-linear model of per-relation cost on structural features of V (predicted exact yield, solving degree, trace and product-space statistics), gate it by the structural yield test (finite expected tuples), and pick the cheapest predicted base from a pool. Unlike the subspace-choice lead (named geometric properties vs a random base), the comparator here is the hand rule (lowest expected solvi

title: Batch IC and IC/rho portfolios: amortising the set-up over many targets, restart portfolios
mechanism: IC pays its set-up once, so per-target cost after set-up falls as 1/L while batch rho falls as 1/sqrt(L); a restart portfolio of IC and rho could exploit heavy tails.

title: Non-subspace Frobenius-stable factor bases at prime n: trace-spectrum, Hamming ball, multiplicative subgroup, tau-adic, algebraic-group (Couveignes-Lercier) poi
mechanism: Prime n with 2 primitive leaves no Frobenius-stable F_2-subspace of useful dimension, but non-linear stable sets exist: V_E = {x : Tr(x^e) = 0, e in E}, Hamming balls in a normal basis, multiplicative subgroups x^d = 1, tau-adic patterns over an orbit-union base, and F_2-rational points of low-dimensional algebraic groups or Jacobians. If one keeps the n-fold orbit gain with a membership system no

title: Gaudry-Diem n = 5 point decomposition on the Oakley EC2N curves over F_{2^155} and F_{2^185}
mechanism: Both RFC 2409 groups are quintic extensions (155 = 5*31, 185 = 5*37), so the subfield base V = F_{2^p} gives a fixed-n = 5 decomposition whose cost is one q-independent Groebner constant K_5 plus a SAT arm priced at q^4.

title: Linear algebra of the orbit-folded relation matrix (equivariant blocks, sparse filters, Wiedemann, CADO-style merge)
mechanism: Exploit the F_r[Z/n]-module structure of the Frobenius-folded relation matrix and sparse methods (filtering, block Wiedemann/Lanczos) to cut the linear-algebra phase.

title: Bounded-degree algebraic decomposition (Weil-descended S_{m+1} on subspace bases) at prime extension degree: ECC2K-130, NIST K/B, sect571
mechanism: The only non-generic oracle on binary curves restricts x_i to an F_2-subspace and solves the Weil-descended S_{m+1} system algebraically. Relation collection beats rho only if a failed attempt costs 2^{alpha l} with alpha < m/2 - 1, which needs refutation at a degree that does not grow with n. title: Quasi-subfield-polynomial factor bases (Huang-Kosters-Petit-Yeo-Yun; Euler-Petit) at prime extension degree, ECC2K-130
mechanism: Roots of X^{2^{n0}} - lambda(X) with small deg lambda give a subspace-like base without an intermediate field, so the summation system could keep low degree at prime n where Frobenius-stable subspaces do not exist.

title: Retained-setup online IC on Koblitz curves (n = 61, 71, 73, 83): online ratio after an uncharged precomputation
mechanism: Precompute the factor-base table and relation logs once, then answer each new target with the descent only. Online-only ratios against rho looked large (13.9x at n61, 18.5x and 54.1x at N83).

title: tau-Horner decomposition chain on Koblitz curves (R = tau^{m-1}P_1 + ... + P_m over one base)
mechanism: Decompose a target as a tau-adic Horner sum of base points, so ordered tuples become distinct relations: the claim is m! times the distinct-relation yield of the plain chain at unchanged descended shape, a constant m! saving on relation collection.

title: Faster Boolean F4 / F5 / F6-IC / inherited-F4 / matrix-F5 engines for the descended Semaev system
mechanism: Engineering of Groebner engines (word-packed XOR, M4RI, bitmaps, signature F5, GPU RREF, learn/apply trace reuse) on the Weil-descended S_3 chain. Engine speedups of 1.4x-2.3x (cryptanalysis) and 1.56x-1.67x (packed residuals) are real, but priced F4 is far above both the pair table and rho at every measured m = 2, 3, 4 cell.

title: Degree of regularity of the Boolean chained Semaev system (m = 3, t = 3) against a semi-regular null
mechanism: GOAL-DREG-001 measures exact GF(2) Macaulay ranks of the descended chained S_3 system and asks whether d_reg(n) departs from the semi-regular prediction; a non-generic departure would make the solving degree, and so the per-query cost, lower than generic models predict. mechanism: Aggregate SDEG/MONO/RELN outputs into one complete-cost IC exponent with a matched rho measured on the same instances, censoring charged and failures included. Audits found the four-size exponent unidentifiable and the 1/2 comparison mis-specified, and enumerative membership, not IC itself, is the bottleneck; the non-enumerative oracle is approved but unbuilt.

title: Does decomposition difficulty change across an isogeny class, curve model or special j (transport to an easier presentation)?
mechanism: Move one ECDLP instance by Velu isogeny, change of model (Weierstrass, Edwards, Montgomery, Hessian) or to a special-j / small-height curve, and look for a presentation whose Semaev system has lower first-fall / solving degree or higher yield. title: Decomposition probability P(decomp) vs factor-base size, charged p_solve, and learned decomposability predictors
mechanism: Index calculus consumes expected charged cost per accepted relation, so P(decomp) must be measured as an exact integer ratio with failures charged, not a sampled scalar. The mean is fixed by yield conservation; only the per-target distribution, clustering and charging remain. Learned predictors (GNN, symbolic regression, learned search policy) were tried as instruments.

title: Does the MutantXL/F4 closure (refutation) degree of descended S_3/S_4 chains stay at 4 as l and n grow?
mechanism: If the solving degree of the Weil-descended decomposition system stays constant (Semaev Assumption 1, Petit-Quisquater FFD), each PDP query is polynomial and binary IC becomes subexponential. Measured: closure degree 3-4 where XL needs 5-7, flat through (m,l) = (4,6) at N = 54, but the degree rises at l = 7 at m = 3. The surviving rule (degree rises at l = 7) sets the ECC2K-130 m = 4 price.

Measured serial-S_3 eliminant exponent stays far above the sub-rho gate.

Every binary merge tree has the same auxiliary and equation counts, and t = m is optimal under the paper's own model.

title: Semaev summation-cover monodromy / Frobenius cycle types as a relation-rate gate
mechanism: If the monodromy of the m-th Semaev cover were smaller than the symmetric/wreath group on some curve family, Chebotarev would give that family a higher relation rate. The geometric monodromy is uniform in the curve: (Z/2)^{m-2} over the ordered base and (Z/2)^{m-2} semidirect S_{m-1} over the symmetric base, and on the factor-base locus the fibre splits completely.

title: Semaev yield model (eq. 11, the m! factor) and coset-typed / trace-parity factor bases
mechanism: Semaev's constant 1.6986 is carried by the m! symmetry of the yield model; coset-typed bases (Nagao-style disjoint shifts) trade m! for a typed domain and could raise yield per query without raising degree. Eq. (11) overstates decomposition probability; trace-parity confinement explains the whole low-degree-window yield deficit.

title: Exploiting the degree-born non-rewritable syzygy (F5 signature) cascade of Semaev systems
mechanism: If the chained Semaev system carries more non-rewritable low-degree syzygies than a generic system, an F5-type solver falls earlier and the solving degree drops. GOAL-SIG-001 counts the D-born non-rewritable signatures; D <= 5 cascades are admissible, the D >= 6 null needs recalibration, and the trivial-syzygy subtraction family itself may be miscounted.

title: Factor bases with low-degree algebraic membership over F_p (subgroup, coset, Dickson, j=0 orbit, images of low-degree maps, character-constant sets)
mechanism: Over F_{q^n} the subfield makes membership x^q = x low degree after Weil restriction. Over F_p one would need a size-B subset cut out by equations of degree << B that survive substitution into S_{m+1} (multiplicative subgroups x^B = 1, cosets, Dickson images, x = g(t)), or a structured base whose multiplicative characters bias x(P +/- Q) and so raise yield.

title: Lifting to characteristic zero - classical xedni, prescribed rational lifts (Cheon 2-isogeny form) and smoothness of integer lifts of x
mechanism: Lift E and the factor-base or target points to E/Q so that rational relations reduce to free relations mod p (xedni), construct rational lifts of a prescribed finite-field pair that are dependent (Cheon-style 2-isogeny family), or treat integer lifts of x(kP) as smooth numbers as in F_p^* index calculus.

title: Harvesting x-key / pair-sum coincidences of structured bases (label-GAP, window, log-GAP) and escaping conservation by target preselection
mechanism: The mitm engine already computes table-table, table-base and search-search x-key collisions; if a structured base carried more pair-sum coincidences than a random base (relation excess kappa > 1), harvesting them would be free relations. A companion idea attempts only targets whose representation x(R) predicts decomposability, since conservation binds only over the whole group.

title: Normal form and calibrated instruments for proposed prime-field attack systems (dedup, result classes, estimator bias, dynamic range)
mechanism: A decidable normal form (base, nvars, degree sequence, Groebner signature, oracle) quotients the many proposed prime-field systems into distinct constructions, and instruments (single-cell exponent estimator, descent detectors) must show unbiasedness and dynamic range before their nulls count. It makes ECDLP cheaper only indirectly, by stopping re-proposal and false nulls.

mechanism: A bilinear map b with b(P, P) nontrivial would turn ECDLP into a DLP in the target group (MOV-like), so residual self-pairing cells (H-PAIR) were re-examined for prime-order curves.

mechanism: Replace number-field lifting by integral sections of rational elliptic surfaces y^2 = x^3 + a(t)x + b(t); specialising t gives points on E/F_p and Mordell-Weil relations among sections specialise to free relations. It helps only if the lift probability decays slower than p^{-1/2} and relation coefficients stay bounded.

title: x-line symmetry groups, automorphism folding and summation-polynomial degeneration at special j
mechanism: The Mobius group preserving the branch set of the x-line has order 4/8/12 (twice Aut), and Macaulay ranks of the summation system can only drop on special loci of (a, b). If a special-j or special coefficient locus dropped rank for an elliptic reason (not a coefficient-block vanishing), its curves would have cheaper decomposition; symmetry folding divides the base by 2, 3 or 6.

title: Rho on E/Aut (negation, j=0 order-6, j=1728 order-4) and anything beyond sqrt(|Aut|)
mechanism: Run Pollard rho on equivalence classes under the automorphism group, which shrinks the search space by |Aut| and the expected steps by sqrt(|Aut|) (sqrt 2 generic, sqrt 4 at j=1728, sqrt 6 at j=0). The EWALK lane asked whether any walk design (orbit-choice mixing, GLV-split walks, full-End quotients) exceeds the sqrt(|Aut|) ceiling.

title: Reduction between Cl(O)-vectorization (or CM self-pairings) and ECDLP in the same class
mechanism: The crater is a Cl(O)-torsor, and curves in the class carry class-group data (edge characters, ray-class fibers, Castryck-Houben-Merz self-pairings). A bridge map could carry a vectorization oracle to an ECDLP solver or back. The ray-class view writes ECDLP on a conductor-1 curve as vectorization inside the fiber of Cl_n(O) -> Cl(O).

mechanism: Generic cost is class-invariant, but IC with a small-abscissa factor base is not: its relation yield depends on which set of points the coordinates call "small". You can transport the instance to the crater (one Velu evaluation per target) or rescale to an isomorphic model whose small-abscissa base gives more relations. This includes the heavy-tail screen for a rare good curve in a class, and the

title: Manipulated generation of standard curves (NIST P-curve seeds, Brainpool, BN, rigidity)
mechanism: If a standard curve's seed or generation procedure was ground, the designer could have selected a curve in a secret weak class. The program regenerated the NIST seeds (drand48 stream, 1997-98) and audited the eleven skipped candidates against the ten published ones. It also audited verifiability and rigidity of other families.

title: Endomorphism-augmented generic and witness-lattice attacks on a prime-order subgroup
mechanism: Give a generic or lattice attack extra oracles or coordinates from efficiently computable endomorphisms (phi(P), phi(Q), eigenvalue relations), hoping the augmented witness lattice or oracle beats the sqrt(N) birthday bound. On a prime-order subgroup G every endomorphism acts as a scalar lambda in Z/N, so each endomorphism adds coordinates but no new congruence.

title: GLV/GLS and isogeny-loop endomorphisms, neighbour-model routing (known-scalar multiplication)
mechanism: Cheap endomorphisms from CM, from isogeny loops on the crater (Koshelev-Sanso) or from a cheaper a=-3 model on an isogenous neighbour speed up variable-base k*P. Several ENDO hypotheses sit under GOAL-ENDO-001 and could be mistaken for ECDLP progress.

title: Generic (rho, BSGS) ECDLP cost across an isogeny class and across volcano levels
mechanism: ECDLP transports along any F_p-isogeny of degree prime to N (T1), so if any curve in the class, at any volcano level or endomorphism-ring depth, were cheaper for rho or BSGS, the whole class would fall. The VOLC lane asked whether depth, level, conductor or a level label read from the group structure changes any measurable generic cost.

title: Multi-target and preprocessing tables shared across an isogeny class
mechanism: Build one preprocessing table (BSGS, Bernstein-Lange distinguished points) on one curve and reuse it for targets on every curve of the class by isogeny transport, amortising precomputation over many curves.

title: Walk or construct isogenies from a deployed curve to find a weak neighbour
mechanism: Enumerate small- and large-degree isogenies from P-256, P-192, P-224 or secp256k1 (millions of models, degrees up to 2^44497-1) and screen each neighbour for a known weakness (anomalous, small embedding degree, small |D|, structure screens). The isogeny-degree records (ISOU) also belong here.

title: Jao-Miller-Venkatesan isogeny-expander random self-reduction within a level
mechanism: JMV (2005) shows, under GRH, that dlog on curves with the same endomorphism ring is randomly self-reducible via short horizontal isogeny walks. The lane asked for its concrete constants and field-operation cost and whether it gives any attack or level-dependent hardness.

title: Curves below a binary Koblitz curve in its volcano (ECC2K-130, K-163, K-283, m=37..83)
mechanism: Descend from a Koblitz curve (D_K = -7, End = Z[tau]) through conductor primes to floor curves. A floor curve might give a cheaper rho or IC than the crater with its Frobenius orbits. The NIST K-163 and K-283 conductor floors are the deployed instances.

title: P-192 isogeny class, smooth principal CM relations and loops
mechanism: Search the valid P-192 isogeny class for short smooth principal CM relations (closed loops) that give a cheap non-scalar endomorphism or a cheap way to navigate the class, then charge it fully to see whether it signals a weakness.

title: SafeCurves-style parameter audits (twist security, completeness, ladder, cofactor, transfer rows)
mechanism: Re-derive the SafeCurves criteria (rho cost, transfer, CM discriminant, twist security, ladder, completeness, indistinguishability) for 20 named curves. Weak rows such as Anomalous show known transfer attacks, and per-curve implementation surfaces (invalid curve, singular companion, cofactor) belong here too.

title: secp256k1 CM structure (D=-3, j=0, h=1) and its isogeny class
mechanism: secp256k1 has j=0, CM by Z[zeta_3], six automorphisms and sextic twists. Its Frobenius conductor is large, so volcanoes sit below it. The audit asked whether its CM, twists, class structure or genus-2 gluings give any route beyond the known sqrt 6 rho factor.

title: Small |D_0| or a cheap non-unit endomorphism beyond the automorphism constant
mechanism: Curves with small CM discriminant (D = -7, -8, -11, ...) or a short CM relation carry cheap endomorphisms of small degree. The hope is that these cheap maps give rho equivalence classes, a smaller crater to search, or another speedup beyond sqrt(|Aut|), even though only D_0 = -3, -4 add units.

title: Special j (0, 1728, small height, Semaev degeneration locus) in Semaev and index-calculus systems
mechanism: At j=0 (a=0) or j=1728 (b=0) the Semaev summation polynomials lose monomials (S_3 support 9 and 10 against 13 generic), and the automorphism group acts on the x-line. A sparser or more symmetric decomposition system might lower the solving degree or the relation cost by more than the sqrt(|Aut|) rho constant. The JINV lane also proposed a Semaev degeneration divisor on the j-line and small-height

title: l-torsion (l != N) as a Galois/End module leaking k or attack cost
mechanism: Division-polynomial factorisation, Elkies/Atkin split patterns, torsion translates and resolvents at primes l != N might carry information about the secret k or about which stage of an attack is cheap. The TORS lane proposed point-dependent statistics such as the Legendre symbol of psi_l(x(kP)).

title: Smart / Satoh-Araki / Semaev p-adic lift for anomalous (trace one) curves
mechanism: When #E(F_p) = p, lifting to E(Q_p) and applying the formal logarithm turns the ECDLP into a linear problem in Z_p (polynomial time). The lift must be a random (non-canonical) one: on the Serre-Tate canonical lift the attack degenerates.

title: Serre-Tate canonical lift with CM: does the CM order shrink the heights of lifted points enough for xedni to bite?
mechanism: The canonical lift of an ordinary curve is a CM curve whose Mordell-Weil group is an O-module; CM might halve the needed points, pin the rank by an L-value or give a structured family of lifts, changing the specific height quantity that kills xedni.

title: Catalogued cover maps (1,940 prime quadratic pullbacks, 160 binary cubic pullbacks): executable pushforward and subgroup recovery
mechanism: The cover catalog lists explicit maps H -> E; executable Jacobian arithmetic, norm maps and subgroup certificates would let any future destination algorithm on H be tested as an ECDLP transfer for the 977 linked EC1 representations.

title: Transfer-safety audits of deployed curves: embedding degree, anomaly, twist, subfield/descent, seed provenance
mechanism: Certify for each standard curve that k is large, #E != p, the field degree is not descent-weak and the parameters were not chosen to land in a weak class (NIST seed reproduction, SafeCurves-style audits).

title: Function-field xedni: lift relations to sections of elliptic surfaces y^2 = x^3 + a(t)x + b(t) over F_p(t)
mechanism: Replace Q by F_p(t): fibre points become values of low-degree integral sections of a rational elliptic surface, where heights are degrees and the Mordell-Weil lattice is E8-like; if a target point lies on a low-degree section with probability p^{-alpha}, alpha < 1/2, sections give an ECDLP relation source.

title: GHS / generalized GHS Weil descent (with Galbraith-Hess-Smart isogeny walks) for curves over F_{2^N}, N composite
mechanism: Weil descent maps E(F_{q^n}) into the Jacobian of a hyperelliptic (or general) curve of small genus over F_q, where index calculus is subexponential; isogeny walks move a curve into the vulnerable part of its class. Weak for N = 5l, 210, partially 3l, 6l, 7l, 8l.

title: Global lifts to E(Q) or E(K) with small canonical height (xedni, SNFS / cyclotomic / Solinas number fields, rational 2-torsion lifts)
mechanism: Lift (E, P, Q) to a curve over Q or a number field and hope the relation between the lifts is a short Mordell-Weil relation, readable from heights or a rank deficiency (Silverman's xedni calculus and its number-field / SNFS variants).

title: Nagao decomposition on a genus-2 cover of E(F_{p^6}) (examples/jv_cover.rs), with F4 and sparse-FGLM engineering
mechanism: Each relation is one Nagao decomposition test solved by F4 then a linear stage; engineering (sparse FGLM, F5 signatures, large-prime variation) lowers the per-test cost and S/rho.

title: Joux-Vitse cover-and-decomposition sieve on the weak class of E(F_{p^6}) (genus-3 cover), with the isogeny walk into the class
mechanism: Curves over F_{p^6} with full rational 2-torsion whose class contains a weak curve admit a genus-3 cover over F_{p^2}; the JV sieve collects relations there at a cost that, in the historical runs, fell far below a strong rho on the same instances.

title: Non-homomorphic transfers into F_p^* when the pairing is trivial: Miller-cocycle primitive U, zeta-defect, generalized Jacobians
mechanism: With gcd(N, p-1) = 1 the Tate pairing is trivial, but the Miller function f_{N,P} yields a canonical map U(R) = f(R)^{1/N} whose coboundary is the line-function cocycle; if log U(kP) carried structure in k (prefix sums of log(x_P - x_{iP})) it would be a cheap non-homomorphic transfer into F_p^*.

title: MOV / Frey-Rueck pairing transfer of the ECDLP to F_{p^k}^* for small embedding degree
mechanism:
The Weil or Tate pairing with an independent N-torsion point maps

injectively into mu_N in F_{p^k}^*, where k = ord_N(p) is the embedding degree; the DLP then falls to finite-field index calculus / (ex)TNFS, subexponential in p^k. It helps only when k is small (supersingular k<=6, pairing-friendly families, CM constructions).

title: Odd-characteristic Weil descent onto genus 3, then Smith's isogeny to a plane quartic and Diem's q^{4/3} attack
mechanism: Descend E/F_{q^3} to a genus-3 hyperelliptic curve over F_q, map it by Smith's (Z/2)^3 isogeny to a non-hyperelliptic plane quartic, and run Diem's double-large-prime index calculus at O~(q^{4/3}) instead of rho's q^{3/2}.

title: Odd-characteristic GHS cover genus floors at prime extension degree and their isogeny-class reach
mechanism: Enumerate Frobenius-orbit branch configurations and cyclic F_2 modules for E/F_(q^n), odd q and prime n, to find low-genus Weil-descent covers; then test which elliptic isogeny classes contain a curve with such a cover.

title: A non-degenerate self-pairing or distortion map computable from one point of the prime-order subgroup
mechanism: If e(P,P) were non-trivial and computable for a single point (via a CM endomorphism acting as a distortion map, or a partial pairing-return cycle), MOV would apply without a second independent N-torsion point, and pairings could give a DDH/ECDLP lever on ordinary prime-field curves.

title: Canonical point sections E(F_p) -> E(Q_p) and their p-adic digits on non-anomalous curves
mechanism: Look for a computable section of reduction on a non-anomalous curve (torsion section, Teichmuller-like or Hensel lifts) whose formal logarithm or p-adic digits linearise the discrete log, generalising Smart beyond trace one.

title: Recompute the post-MOV target-field DLP cost (exTNFS in GF(p^12)) for BLS12-381 and BN254 with memory charged
mechanism: For pairing curves the ECDLP is bounded by the DLP in GF(p^k) after MOV; the quoted 128/100-bit labels come from one family of exTNFS estimates. Running the polynomial selection, charging linear-algebra memory and descent, and reporting the tail over selections could move the effective security of the transferred problem.

title: Isogeny transfer of a prime-field ECDLP to a weaker curve (anomalous, low embedding degree, descent-friendly) in the same class
mechanism: A coprime-degree isogeny transports logs exactly; if a short path led from a generic curve to a special one, the special-curve attack plus the path cost could beat rho.

title: Embed E/F_p as an isogeny factor of a genus-g Jacobian over the same field (covers, quadric pencils, quartic/bielliptic models)
mechanism: Map the ECDLP into the Jacobian of a curve C over the same field with Jac(C) ~ E x A (a cover C -> E, a bielliptic quartic, a surface or quadric-pencil model) and use genus-g index calculus there.

title: Reach a second N-torsion direction: nonequivariant trace-zero transfer, Kani/Robert graph kernels, Richelot gluing of E with E'
mechanism: Move the rational N-torsion line into a Frobenius-nontrivial direction (trace-zero variety T_k(E)) or build an (N,N) graph kernel in E x E' to embed into a principally polarised surface (Castryck-Decru / Robert machinery), then decompose or walk there.

title: Find small-genus GHS/Kummer covers beyond the Joux-Vitse weak class (other configurations over F_{q^3}, F_{p^k} with k = 6, 10, 14)
mechanism: If curves outside the JV class, or over other extension degrees, had covers of genus <= 3 (or genus g with q^{2-2/g} below rho), the cover attack would extend to more of the curve population.

title: Teske-style trapdoor on ordinary prime-field curves: a secret isogeny to an endpoint with a non-invariant ECDLP weakness
mechanism: Teske's binary trapdoor hides a GHS-weak curve behind a secret isogeny. Over F_p, the analogue needs a weakness that varies inside one isogeny class (Semaev/factor-base yield, Macaulay degrees, conductor level) and is not publicly recognisable.

title: Teske-style trapdoor over F_{p^6} built on the Joux-Vitse weak class
mechanism: Over prime fields, Tate's theorem leaves an isogeny trapdoor nothing to hide. Over F_{p^6}, Joux-Vitse weakness belongs to individual curves rather than whole isogeny classes: only 55-63% of classes contain a weak curve, and the ISO-1 walk reaches one. That is the structure Teske's binary-field trapdoor uses. A search of crypto's research reports found no trapdoor work on F_{p^6} or JV.

title: Genus-n Jacobians in the isogeny class of a Weil-restricted elliptic curve
mechanism: Search for a genus-n curve C/F_q whose Jacobian is isogenous to Res_(F_(q^n)/F_q) E, including classes missed by the explicit GHS x-line cover. Existence alone supplies no computable DLP transfer.
